items.name: Menza
items.hours: Daily c. 11:00-23:00 (kitchen to ~22:30; sources vary). Open Thu/Fri/Sat late and Sun lunch. Confirm on the day.
items.blurb: Retro 70s canteen chic on Liszt Ferenc tér. Hungarian classics, a proper wine list and people-watching from the terrace. Good first-night shout for a big group.
items.tip: Hortobágyi palacsinta (savoury pancakes in veal paprikash). Book ahead for Fri/Sat dinner for 6+.

items.name: Café Kör
items.hours: Mon-Sat approx 10:00/12:00-22:00; CLOSED Sunday (sources differ on opening time). Fine Thu-Sat.
items.blurb: Tiny, buzzing bistro behind the Basilica where locals actually eat. Proper Hungarian cooking, no gimmicks. Fits a big lads' table only if you book.
items.tip: Go for the daily specials board. Reservations are essentially always needed, so book days ahead.

items.name: Kispiac Bisztró
items.hours: Mon-Sat approx 12:00-22:00; closed Sun (one source also says Mon). Check before going.
items.blurb: Six-table shoebox of a bistro by Hold Street market hall. Unfussy pork, liver and offal done properly. Tiny, so only for a small group or an early lunch.
items.tip: Breaded veal liver, pork belly or the wild boar ribs. Book at least two days ahead; walk-ins rarely get in.

items.name: Frici Papa Kifőzdéje
items.hours: Listing says ~11:00-23:00 (kitchen may stop earlier), closed Sun - listing dated, so confirm. No bookings.
items.blurb: Budapest's cheapest sit-down Hungarian dinner since 1997. Canteen tables, shared benches, big plates, tiny bill. Perfect for a hangover or a pre-bar fill-up.
items.tip: Daily menu (under ~3,000 HUF per tourism guide), főzelék or pörkölt with nokedli. Cash preferred; no booking.

items.name: Gettó Gulyás
items.hours: Opening hours not verified; guides say reserve, no walk-ins after 19:00. Small room.
items.blurb: Old-school Hungarian grub in the Jewish Quarter. Goulash, stuffed cabbage and the famous túrógombóc, in a room too small for a stag-sized mob.
items.tip: Goulash plus túrógombóc (cottage-cheese dumplings). Reserve a day ahead; best for groups of 4 or fewer.

items.name: Hungarikum Bisztró
items.hours: Daily approx 12:00-14:30 and 18:00-22:00 (sources vary). Online reservation recommended.
items.blurb: Hearty, no-nonsense Hungarian a stone's throw from Parliament. Goulash soup, paprikash and strudel, served by people who know what they're doing.
items.tip: Gulyásleves then chicken paprikás with nokedli. Small room, so book online for lunch or dinner.

items.name: Pörc & Prézli
items.hours: Hours not verified for 2026 - check Google Maps. Usually busiest Sat evening.
items.blurb: Pork, duck and goose in a lively room next to the Opera. Loud, proper portions, occasionally pricey service charge. A new sister bistro (Pici Pörc) opened opposite in Aug 2026.
items.tip: Duck breast or goose with something hearty. Almost always fully booked, so reserve well ahead.

items.name: Kéhli Vendéglő
items.hours: Mon-Fri 12:00-22:00, Sat 12:00-22:30, Sun 12:00-21:00 (one source) - good for Sunday lunch.
items.blurb: Old Óbuda tavern, famed for bone marrow and a Krúdy-era vibe. Out of the centre, but worth the taxi if you want proper Hungarian portions on a lazy Sunday.
items.tip: Bone marrow with toast, then a big meaty main. Take a taxi or tram; book for 6+.

items.name: Kőleves Vendéglő
items.hours: Hours vary by source (about 11:30-23:00 daily); weekday lunch menu until 16:00. Confirm.
items.blurb: Jewish Quarter staple with a leafy garden next door. Hungarian-meets-modern plates, decent for a group who can't agree.
items.tip: Lunch menu on weekdays is good value. Ask for the garden if it's dry.

items.name: Fülemüle Étterem
items.hours: Hours not verified - check before going.
items.blurb: Cosy old-school place for Jewish-Hungarian classics near Astoria/Blaha. Lescó, goose liver and sólet, none of it light.
items.tip: Sólet (bean and meat stew) or fried goose liver. Call ahead for a group.

items.name: Mazel Tov
items.hours: Official site: Mon-Fri 12:00-23:00, Sat-Sun 10:30-00:00. Open late Thu-Sat; Sun brunch/lunch available.
items.blurb: Gorgeous Mediterranean courtyard in a Jewish Quarter ruin. Middle Eastern sharing plates, great cocktails, perfect for a big group night out.
items.tip: Shakshuka for brunch, mezze to share. Book a week ahead for weekends; card issues reported, bring cash backup.

items.name: Stand25 Bisztró
items.hours: Mon-Sat 12:00-16:00 and 17:30-24:00 per Michelin; CLOSED Sunday. Still listed in Michelin 2024/25 - verify 2026.
items.blurb: Refined Hungarian from the Stand team in a relaxed bistro, Michelin Plate. Buda side, so a short taxi from VII. Not the cheapest feed but proper nosh.
items.tip: Go for the Hungarian classics tasting-style plates. Book ahead and check it is still open at this address.

items.name: Stand
items.hours: Tue-Sat 18:00-00:00; closed Sun and Mon. Open Thu/Fri/Sat evenings.
items.blurb: Budapest's only two-Michelin-star restaurant. Dinner, not a meal: smart Hungarian tasting menus. Put the good shirt on, lads.
items.tip: Tasting menu only. Bookings open about 60 days ahead (SevenRooms) and tables are held for 20 mins. Probably sold out by now - try cancellations.

items.name: Borkonyha Winekitchen
items.hours: Mon-Fri from 18:00, Sat 12:00-24:00; closed Sun. Open Thu/Fri/Sat; no Sunday service.
items.blurb: One-star Hungarian by the Basilica. Slick but unstuffy, huge Hungarian wine list. The best 'treat ourselves' dinner without tipping into silly.
items.tip: Tasting menu over à la carte. Book online 2-4 weeks ahead for weekends; try for a Sat lunch slot at short notice.

items.name: Rumour by Rácz Jenő
items.hours: Tue-Sat 17:00-23:00; closed Sun and Mon. Counter seating (21 seats).
items.blurb: Michelin-starred 21-seat chef's counter hidden behind an unmarked door. Eleven courses of modern Hungarian with theatre. Address reported two ways - check booking email.
items.tip: Eleven-course counter tasting (roughly 60,000-85,000 HUF). Book about 3 weeks ahead; arrive early.

items.name: Costes
items.hours: One guide: Wed-Sun evenings approx 18:30-24:00; closed Mon/Tue. Hours conflict - confirm directly.
items.blurb: Hungary's first Michelin-star restaurant (2010), on the buzzy Ráday utca. Elegant tasting menus, quality service. Dress to impress.
items.tip: Tasting menu. Phone line takes bookings daily 9:00-23:30. Book now, weekends fill fast.

items.name: Babel
items.hours: Tue-Fri 17:30-24:00, Sat 12:00-15:00 and evening; closed Sun and Mon.
items.blurb: One Michelin star since 2019, tucked near Elisabeth Bridge. Modern Hungarian with a bit of flair. Sat lunch is the lads-friendly slot before footy.
items.tip: Saturday lunch tasting menu. Book online; ask about a lunch slot if dinner is gone.

items.name: Bors GasztroBár
items.hours: About 11:30-21:00 Mon-Thu/Sun, to 22:00 Fri-Sat (sources vary). Expect a queue at lunch.
items.blurb: Tiny soup-and-baguette bar with Star Wars decor and ridiculous queues for good reason. Cheap, cheerful and next to the ruin pubs.
items.tip: Daily soup or a stuffed baguette. Eat at the counter or take it away; no booking.

items.name: Zing Burger (Karaván)
items.hours: Karaván courtyard open daily 11:30-23:59 (reports of 01:00 Thu-Sat). Other branches have longer hours.
items.blurb: Budapest's home-grown burger chain. Smashed burgers, no frills, handy when beers are flowing next door.
items.tip: Classic double cheeseburger and fries. Loyalty-card stamps if you're round for the weekend.

items.name: Pampas Steakhouse
items.hours: Daily approx 12:00-23:00 (one listing shows Thu-Sat 23:00, Mon-Wed/Sun 22:00). Book for Sat night.
items.blurb: Argentine-style steakhouse, glossy and meaty. Dozen-plus premium cuts, big wine list. OpenTable rating 4.6-4.8 across ~550-600 reviews.
items.tip: Choose your cut from the trolley and share sides. Book via OpenTable; mains from about 50 EUR.

items.name: Belli di Mamma
items.hours: Listing (unclear): Mon-Thu 17:00-23:00, Fri-Sun 12:00-23:00. Confirm. Open Sun lunch.
items.blurb: Only Hungarian pizzeria in Europe's Top 50 (No. 40, 2026). Proper Neapolitan pies, right in the party district. Lads can argue over toppings later.
items.tip: Order a margherita first and judge them on that. Pies roughly 3,700-6,300 HUF. Book for 6+.

items.name: Bp BARbq
items.hours: Old listing: daily 11:00-24:00. Moved to this address on 6 Oct 2026 - recheck hours.
items.blurb: Texas-style brisket, ribs and wings. Just moved from Akácfa to Hercegprímás utca (opened 6 Oct 2026). Smoky, sticky and sociable.
items.tip: Brisket sandwich or a ribs platter to share. New site, so check it is open and Google Maps pin.

items.name: Retró Lángos Büfé
items.hours: Reported daily 11:00-22:00 (one source says 9:00). Address conflicts between sources (Arany János u. 9) - confirm.
items.blurb: Lángos central: crispy fried dough piled high with garlic, sour cream and cheese. The textbook belly-liner.
items.tip: Classic lángos (about 3,500 HUF in 2026). Add extra garlic, regret nothing.

items.name: Karaván Street Food
items.hours: Daily 11:30-23:59 (Sep 2026 guide); another says to 01:00 Thu-Sat. Open Sun.
items.blurb: Courtyard of food trucks and bars next to Szimpla. Lángos, burgers, gyros, chimney cake, all in one gloriously chaotic pit-stop.
items.tip: Lángos, a burger truck, and a chimney cake for pudding. Easy to split a group across trucks.

items.name: Szimply
items.hours: Mon-Sat approx 9:00-16:00 (8:00 start claimed); closed Sundays. Good for Fri/Sat hangover brunch.
items.blurb: Relaxed, light-filled brunch place from the Szimpla family in a historic alley. Eggs, coffee, juices and recovery vibes.
items.tip: Eggs Benedict or a big brunch plate. No Sunday service, so don't plan the post-match recovery here.

items.name: Szimpla Kert Sunday Market
items.hours: Sundays: Szimpla opens ~9:00; farmers market approx 9:00-14:00/15:00 (sources vary).
items.blurb: The famous ruin pub turns into a Sunday farmers market, with cheese, honey, jam and street food stalls. Ideal if you're up for Sunday brunch.
items.tip: Browse stalls then grab brunch upstairs. Check opening times on the day (the end time varies).

items.name: Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok)
items.hours: Mon-Fri 6:00-18:00, Sat 6:00-16:00 (most sources). Sunday: Oct 2026 guide says 10:00-16:00 but older/official English page say closed - confirm. Lángos upstairs.
items.blurb: Neo-Gothic food cathedral. Paprika, sausages, pálinka downstairs; lángos and goulash upstairs. Do it Saturday morning before the footy.
items.tip: Upstairs: lángos and goulash (touristy). Downstairs: sausage, salami, paprika to take home. Go before 13:00 on Saturday.

items.name: Hold Street Market Hall (Belvárosi Piac)
items.hours: Mon 6:30-17:00, Tue-Fri 6:30-18:00, Sat 6:30-14:00/16:00 (sources vary); closed Sunday. One listing flagged it temporarily closed - verify.
items.blurb: 1891 market hall with a food gallery of small kitchens upstairs. Quieter and more local than the Great Market Hall.
items.tip: Browse for lunch Saturday morning. Verify it is open as a Google Maps flag showed it as temporarily closed.

items.name: Kelet Kávézó
items.hours: Weekdays approx 7:30-22:00/23:00, weekends 9:00-22:00/23:00 (sources vary).
items.blurb: Bookish Buda café-gallery with good filter coffee, bagels and savoury plates. A calm recovery spot away from Pest.
items.tip: Order and pay at the counter. Savoury brunch plate and a filter coffee. Sat/Sun mornings after 9.

items.name: Molnár's Kürtőskalács
items.hours: Daily approx 10:00-22:00 (single source).
items.blurb: Famous chimney cake stall on Váci utca. Warm, sugary, cinnamon-dusted spiral of joy to eat while strolling.
items.tip: Cinnamon or walnut chimney cake. Ask for it fresh from the grill and watch the bake.

items.name: Café Gerbeaud
items.hours: Approx 9:00-20:00 (to 21:00 Fri/Sat), sources vary. Open all weekend.
items.blurb: Grand 1858 confectioner on Vörösmarty tér. Touristy, pricey, gorgeous. Come for cake and a coffee-house atmosphere.
items.tip: Dobos torta or Somlói galuska. 15% service charge reported. Skip the queue and sit inside.

dishes.name: Gulyás
dishes.what: Beef, paprika, spuds. Not the brown mush you get back home. Order the soup, not the stew, unless you want a stew.
dishes.whereText: Gettó Gulyás, Menza, Hungarikum, Frici Papa

dishes.name: Pörkölt
dishes.what: Thick paprika stew of beef or pork, served with nokedli. Goulash's heartier mate.

dishes.name: Paprikás csirke
dishes.what: Chicken in creamy paprika sauce with dumplings. Basically a Sunday roast hug.

dishes.name: Halászlé
dishes.what: Fiery red river-fish soup, loaded with paprika. A proper dare if you're hungover.
dishes.whereText: Traditional Hungarian restaurants, ask for it by name

dishes.name: Töltött káposzta
dishes.what: Cabbage rolls stuffed with pork and rice, in a smoky sauce with sour cream. Grandma's dinner.

dishes.name: Lángos
dishes.what: Fried dough, garlic, sour cream, cheese. Hangover legend and the best cheap feed in town.
dishes.whereText: Retró Lángos, Karaván, Great Market Hall

dishes.name: Kürtőskalács
dishes.what: Spiral cake roasted over charcoal, rolled in sugar and cinnamon. Peel and eat, no cutlery.

dishes.name: Túró Rudi
dishes.what: Curd cheese bar in dark chocolate. The nation's favourite snack; grab from any shop.
dishes.whereText: Any Spar, Tesco or corner shop

dishes.name: Dobos torta
dishes.what: Six sponge layers, chocolate buttercream, hard caramel lid. Invented in Budapest in 1885.

dishes.name: Rétes
dishes.what: Paper-thin pastry rolled with apple, cherry or curd. Best warm, with a coffee.

dishes.name: Főzelék
dishes.what: Thick veg stew with a fried egg or meatball on top. Cheap, filling, oddly good.

dishes.name: Hurka és kolbász
dishes.what: Smoky sausage and rice or liver pudding. Meaty and unapologetic. Paprika-heavy.

dishes.name: Libamáj
dishes.what: Rich goose liver, pan-seared or in pâté. Fine dining on a budget.

dishes.name: Somlói galuska
dishes.what: Sponge, chocolate sauce, rum, whipped cream and nuts. Dessert for people who don't do dessert.

dishes.name: Unicum
dishes.what: Herbal bitter, 40% ABV, tastes like medicine. Hungarians sip it after dinner and swear it cures everything.

dishes.name: Pálinka
dishes.what: Fruit brandy, fierce and fragrant. Apricot, plum or pear. Sip, don't shoot it.

dishes.name: Fröccs
dishes.what: Wine plus soda water. Cheap, refreshing, and a proper session drink. Try a háztartási or kisfröccs.

dishes.name: Tokaji aszú
dishes.what: Golden sweet wine from the Tokaj region, loved by kings. Sip after dinner.

dishes.name: Dreher / Soproni
dishes.what: Hungarian lagers. Dreher is the classic; Soproni is a fixture. Cheap, cold, fine for a session.
